findings.reason: the plan should either parameterise the existing writer or state why the two edge types cannot share one guarded write, which is exactly the count-guard duplication §8 exists to remove.
findings.text: §8's new consolidated MAPS_TO_IMAS writer would duplicate `write_candidates`'s mechanism (write the edge batch, compare the returned count against the expected count, raise on shortfall; graph_ops.py:605-620), differing only in relationship type and payload properties, and the plan nowhere says why `write_candidates` cannot be generalised over (relationship type, property payload, expected-count semantics) instead of a parallel function being added

findings.reason: the count should move beside `write_candidates` in graph_ops.py so `discover status`, `discover clear` and `imas map status` all read one owner, which is the single-owner rule §8 applies to the MAPS_TO_IMAS edge.
findings.text: `count_candidates_by_route` is a candidate-state reader that §8 relies on for `imas map status` reuse, yet §8's own node rule states "No candidate query is written in workers.py or mapping.py" while placing the other three candidate operations (`write_candidates`, `clear_candidates`, and the new `read_candidates`/`select_candidate`) in imas_codex/ids/graph_ops.py, so candidate-state ownership is split across two modules and workers.py (the claim-loop module) is a second owner

response_events.reason: The two writers share only a three-line count comparison. write_candidates deletes a source's prior MAPPING_CANDIDATE edges, writes the new set, sets candidate_route under a CASE guard and releases the claim in one statement. The MAPS_TO_IMAS writer upserts bindings with transform properties and touches no route or claim. A generic writer would interpolate the relationship type and merge two different replace semantics behind flags, which adds indirection without removing any logic.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — imas_codex/ids/candidates.py (479 lines) hides embedding, per-arm retrieval, arm-merge, decisions-code judgment and threshold routing behind `retrieve_candidates`/`route_ids`/`judge_candidates`/`route` plus three frozen dataclasses that compose `SearchHit` rather than copy it; §8 keeps all candidate-edge lifecycle in one module (imas_codex/ids/graph_ops.py), which is depth, not spread.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the candidate-state reader §8 depends on lives outside the module §8 itself declares owns every candidate query.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §8 is net-negative surface and names its retirements in its own text: it deletes `compute_semantic_matches` (imas_codex/ids/tools.py:769), deletes `count_sources_by_mapping_status` (imas_codex/ids/workers.py:434, verified callerless), removes two `imas map run` options (`--skip-metadata`, `--skip-errors`) and two SignalSource fields, so its two added functions (`read_candidates`, `select_candidate`) are accounted for by the functions they retire.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan cites and extends existing mechanisms throughout: `hybrid_dd_search` for retrieval (imas_codex/graph/dd_search.py:97), shared `call_decisions` (imas_codex/discovery/base/llm.py) for pair judgment, `fetch_wiki_context`/`fetch_code_context`/`fetch_cross_facility_mappings` (imas_codex/ids/tools.py:638/681/733), the generalised claim routines in imas_codex/discovery/base/claims.py for §7, and `PipelineCost` for §10; §8's only new machinery is a per-source candidate-edge reader and the consolidated MAPS_TO_IMAS writer, both of which have no prior owner.
